science.title: Rapid bacterial community profiling of equine microbiomes using Oxford Nanopore sequencing

This research aims to understand how the foal gut microbiome develops by investigating the microbiomes of mares and their foals.

science.title: Electyrolyzer experiment designated ready-to-fly by NASA
science.description: A Southwest Research Institute and University of Texas at San Antonio experiment has passed a critical NASA review, designating it ready for parabolic flight testing. The two institutions will evaluate the performance of a patent-pending electrolyzer, the Mars Atmospheric Reactor for Synthesis of Consumables (MARS-C), in partial-gravity environments.

science.title: Does dark energy really exist? Our work identifies cracks in the foundations of today's cosmological model
science.description: According to current understanding, the universe is expanding—and is doing so at an accelerating rate. This is believed to be caused by something called the cosmological constant, which was first proposed by Albert Einstein in his theory of general relativity. In recent decades, it has become better known as dark energy, which is believed to make up about 70% of the universe.

science.title: Astronomers found a planet 63 light-years away that appears as blue as Earth from space-but its colour comes from a scorching atmosphere where glass may rain sideways in 4,500-mile-per-hour winds

science.title: The ISS toilet costs $23 million and separates urine into a centrifuge that recycles 98% of it back into drinking water - a closed-loop system that took NASA 40 years to perfect
science.description: The $23 million toilet on the International Space Station feeds a centrifuge-driven water recycler that reclaims 98 percent of urine, sweat, and cabin humidity — a closed-loop system NASA spent four decades getting right.

science.title: Every winter, a single beluga whale in the Arctic will dive to 700 metres and stay under for 25 minutes on a lungful of air compressed to 1/70th its surface volume, sustained by muscles so oxygen-rich
science.description: A beluga can dive 700 metres beneath Arctic ice on a single breath, its lungs folding down under pressure and its muscle running on stored oxygen. The physiology that lets one of the ocean's most vocal animals live in near-total darkness — and the world it was built for, which is now vanishing.
